title: The Old Man and Death
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: An Old Man cut himself a bundle of faggots in a wood and started to carry them home. He had a long way to go, and was tired out before he had got much more than half-way. Casting his burden on the ground, he called upon Death to come and release him from his life of toil.

The words were scarcely out of his mouth when, much to his dismay, Death stood before him and professed his readiness to serve him. He was almost frightened out of his wits, but he had enough presence of mind to stammer out, "Good sir, if you'd be so kind, pray help me up with my burden again."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Old Man cut in the wood?
options: A load of firewood logs
A basket of fruit
A bundle of faggots
A pile of stones

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how far does the Old Man get before growing tired?
options: Much more than half-way
Only a few steps from the wood
All the way to his home
Less than a quarter of the way

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Old Man do with his burden when he grows tired?
options: He hides it behind a tree
He gives it to a passerby
He sets it on fire
He casts it on the ground

questions.prompt: According to the passage, whom does the Old Man call upon for release from his toil?
options: A passing traveller
Death
The gods of the forest
His own family

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does Death respond to being called?
options: Death ignores the call entirely
Death sends a messenger instead of appearing
Death stands before him and professes readiness to serve him
Death laughs and disappears

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Old Man ask Death to do instead?
options: Help him up with his burden again
Carry him the rest of the way home
Explain why he appeared so suddenly
Wait until he finishes his journey

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Old Man change his mind so quickly once Death actually appears?
options: He realizes Death has come to the wrong person by mistake
He wants to bargain with Death for more time
He is angry that Death took so long to arrive
His wish for death was only a passing complaint, not something he truly meant

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Old Man's reaction reveal about complaints made in a moment of exhaustion?
options: Such complaints always reflect a person's deepest true wishes
Such complaints may not reflect what a person truly wants when tested
Such complaints are usually taken literally by those who hear them
Such complaints have no real consequences at all

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "toil" mean in "his life of toil"?
options: Peaceful rest
Sudden danger
Hard, wearying work
Quiet celebration

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: People often wish for an escape from hardship without truly meaning it, as they discover when the wish nearly comes true
Old age always brings a genuine wish to die
Death responds instantly to anyone who calls for it
Carrying heavy burdens should always be avoided

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where does the Old Man cut the bundle of faggots?
options: Beside a river
In his own garden
On a rocky hillside
In a wood

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how quickly does Death appear after being called?
options: After a long delay of several hours
The words were scarcely out of the Old Man's mouth
Only after the Old Man called several times
The next morning

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the Old Man address Death in his request?
options: "Dear friend"
"Mighty one"
"Good sir"
"Kind stranger"

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why is it significant that Death "professed his readiness to serve" the Old Man?
options: It takes the Old Man's earlier wish literally and offers to grant it at once
It shows that Death was already planning to visit him regardless
It suggests Death was reluctant to answer the call
It proves the Old Man had summoned Death many times before

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the phrase "enough presence of mind" suggest about the Old Man's state when he replies?
options: He is completely calm and unaffected by Death's appearance
He has lost all ability to think or speak clearly
He had planned his reply well before Death ever appeared
Despite his fear, he manages to think clearly enough to redirect the request

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "stammer" mean in "stammer out"?
options: To shout loudly and clearly
To speak with hesitation or difficulty
To whisper very softly
To remain completely silent

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: An Old Man successfully asks Death to end his life
Death refuses to appear when the Old Man calls for him
An exhausted Old Man calls for Death out of frustration, then quickly asks for help with his load instead once Death appears
An Old Man is punished by Death for complaining about his burden
